tb21_profile.skill: Deduce an exact nn.Module architecture from a state_dict's keys and tensor shapes, load it strictly, freeze every layer but one, optimize only that layer's parameters to lower MSE, and re-serialize as TorchScript with state-dict key compatibility preserved
tb21_profile.domain: PyTorch: state dicts, nn.Module construction, requires_grad/optimizer parameter groups, torch.jit TorchScript export, MSE regression
tb21_profile.task_form: recover-from-artifact then constrained repair: rebuild the lost definition, change exactly one layer, prove the rest is byte-identical, and re-export

verifier_notes: model-training_20260618_093107_003 is graded `weak` (strength 0.2) but I read tests/test_outputs.py: 4 of its 5 tests are substantive - it torch.jit.loads /app/model.pt and checks output shape, asserts every intact key is allclose to the corrupted checkpoint at atol=1e-6, asserts every corrupted key changed, and requires held-out cross-entropy below 0.9x the corrupted model's. The heuristic undercounted it; I treat it as ok/strong and rank it first. model-training_20260604_193056_003 is the single closest instruction match in the whole pool ('infer the architecture from the checkpoint's state dict, fix corrupted parameters without altering intact ones, train to val MSE < 1.30') but is graded FREE, so it is ranked in per_source and kept out of final_top10.

notes: CalibForge is transformative here: its contrastive_solver split contains a whole `recover a PyTorch model from a damaged checkpoint` family, including model-training_20260618_093107_003, which matches pytorch-model-recovery step for step (deduce architecture from state dict, freeze intact layers, tune only the rest, save TorchScript to /app/model.pt, do not modify the source file). Nothing in the v1 pool comes close on the TorchScript or freeze-and-tune axes - `tools.py search all 'TorchScript|torch.jit'` returns exactly one v1 hit. TMax is still a good second source for the state-dict-to-architecture deduction. Terminal-Lego contributes only the requires_grad / per-layer-parameter mechanics at toy depth and has no TorchScript content at all. Recursive-Task-Synthesis could not field 10 defensible candidates: ranks 8-10 are SQLAlchemy `model.py` lexical matches with overall 1, and the whole corpus has four PyTorch mentions. TerminalWorld is similarly thin - one real PyTorch task (tw_718060) and then environment chores. SWE-Smith's entire contribution is the fvcore repo, which is genuinely useful (checkpoint loading, torch.jit analysis, selective BN-buffer updates) but loses on task_form as expected.
